text:
sophia: FYI — onboarding Sparkplug's LoRA finetune hit a weird regression after int4 quant. Quick check pls? :eyes:
aj: seeing this too, can you paste the failing examples?
marco: brief summary — after we merged the LoRA into base v1.3 and ran quantize->int4 pipeline, accuracy on the customer QA set dropped ~6% EM, generation length shortened. Logs attached below.
sophia: sample failing prompt: 
```
Input: "Summarize the support ticket about payment retries"
Expected: long structured bullets with amounts and next steps
Output: 2 short sentences, missed amounts
```
kai: do we have tokenizer mismatch between finetune repo and runtime? Tokenizer shifts often cause truncation after quant.
marco: checked — same tokenizer checkpoint, but the LoRA training used a pad token override and experimental embedding remap. That could interact with quantized KV cache indices.
aj: can you run the quick eval pack I pushed to the S3 bucket? s3://redwood-evals/sparkplug/quickpack-2026-03-21.tar.gz — it contains the devset + unit prompts and an int4/int8/fp16 sweep harness.
sophia: kicking the sweep now — running `./eval_harness --model base_v1.3+sparkplug-lora --quant int4 --batch 16 --timeout 1200`
dev-bot: eval job 98721 queued on cluster-gpu-pool-a, estimate 12m
marco: also run with cache warmstart enabled: `--warm_cache true` — we saw int4 regressions often disappear with KV warmstart on similar merges.
kai: if warmstart doesn't fix it, try re-merging LoRA with `--compat-mode strict-token-map` (there's a helper in ml/tools/merge_lora.py). That will remap any override tokens to base indices.
sophia: first sweep results (int4 / warmstart=false): EM drop 5.9%, avg reply length -28%. int8: EM drop 0.7%. fp16: baseline.
lucy: re-run with warmstart=true results?
sophia: warmstart=true int4 run done: EM drop 1.1%, length -6% — much better. Looks like KV cache warmstart is masking a remap issue but not fully fixing it.
marco: this suggests the LoRA introduced token-id aliasing for pad/sep; warmstart restores proper KV alignment at runtime but some edge cases still truncate.
aj: plan proposal: 1) ship a quick rollback to int8 for Sparkplug (safest), 2) re-merge LoRA with `strict-token-map`, 3) add a small preflight in onboarding that runs int4 + warmstart on the customer's devset and checks length/EM deltas > threshold.
kai: agree. Also add a Redwood Optimize suggestion that flags pad/token overrides in uploaded LoRAs. Preventative rule: reject upload if token remap present unless opt-in.
sophia: created quick rollback PR to routing to prefer int8 for customer sparkplug (PR 8342). Can someone review? :thumbsup:
marco: reviewing now. Quick note — include the evalpack snapshot in the PR description with the int4/warmstart numbers.
aj: ops: schedule a short maintenance window to flip routing for Sparkplug at 03:00 UTC if PR passes tests.
lucy: logging checklist for follow-up: 1) save evalpack artifacts to experiment store, 2) add tokenizer remap detector in upload pipeline, 3) add a smoke test to onboarding that runs the quickpack (int4 warmstart) and fails CI if avg length drops >10%.
sophia: adding items to onboarding ticket ENGML-2124. Thanks all.
dev-bot: Canary deploy of routing change to stage succeeded (stage.sparkplug -> int8 preference).
aj: after we re-merge with strict-token-map, let's re-run int4+warmstart and validate on the full QA set before removing the int8 guard.
kai: I'll take the strict-merge and small unit test to detect pad/sep aliasing. ETA EOD.
marco: nice coordinated response, thanks. :rocket:
